text:
Lawson Crouse scored 24 goals last season. This season he has two, and the reason is mostly the puck refusing to go in. He has 4.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances) on 32 shots and is shooting 6.2%, less than half his usual rate.

Underneath, Utah is fine with him out there. The Mammoth take 58% of the expected goals at five-on-five in his minutes, better than without him, and he's still creating 0.83 expected goals per 60, a bit below last season's 0.95. His goal against Vegas on Wednesday was a typical one: a point shot hit traffic, the rebound bounced to him, and he backhanded it into an open net from a sharp angle, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger described it.

He's doing the heavy work too, with 49 hits in 20 games. Evolving-Hockey valued him at 1.4 wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense. And Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found a passer hidden in there: 18% of his setups cross the royal road, against 7% for a typical forward.

His minutes sit near 15 a night. Goals tend to follow chances like these.
